title: How To Blunt Blood Sugar Spikes Without Fear-Mongering About Breakfast
topic: Breakfast choices, oats, and practical ways to reduce blood sugar spikes
description: A low-risk pilot topic focused on practical blood-sugar management tactics and a fact-check of oversimplified anti-oatmeal breakfast claims.

sources.title: Blunt Blood Sugar Spikes without Cutting Carbs
sources.summary: Practical, food-based tactics to reduce post-meal glucose spikes without eliminating carbohydrates entirely.
key_points: Adding protein to a carbohydrate-heavy meal can blunt the glucose response.
Apple cider vinegar is framed as another tactic that may reduce spikes before meals.
Food order, whole grains, cooling starches, and lentils are presented as practical levers.

sources.title: "Stop Eating this Breakfast!" | Dr. Mark Hyman Fact-Checked
sources.summary: A fact-check of a breakfast claim that portrays oatmeal as harmful, arguing that the cited comparison is really about glycemic index, fiber, and meal composition rather than oats versus eggs in isolation.
key_points: The original viral framing says oatmeal is one of the worst breakfasts and compares it against omelets.
The fact-check argues the cited study is not a clean eggs-versus-oats comparison.
The transcript explicitly says unprocessed oats can still be a healthy breakfast and criticizes fear-mongering.
